name: Implementing End-to-End Security Controls for Cloud and AI Workloads
outlineVersion: Skills measured: study guide last updated 2026-05-13 (no explicit 'skills measured as of' date shown)

exam.notes: Earns Microsoft Certified: Cloud and AI Security Engineer Associate, successor to Azure Security Engineer Associate (AZ-500), which retired August 31, 2026 (exam, cert and renewals). Beta from ~May/June 2026; reported generally available (out of beta) by late July 2026. 120 minutes exam time (official certification page); +30 minutes available if not in preferred language. Practice assessment not yet available. No formal prerequisites; recommended Azure/hybrid admin, Entra ID and Microsoft 365 admin familiarity.

caveats: Outline fetched from the official SC-500 study guide (page last updated 2026-05-13; no explicit skills-measured date shown). SC-500 earns Microsoft Certified: Cloud and AI Security Engineer Associate and is the successor to AZ-500 (Azure Security Engineer Associate), which retired August 31, 2026 per Microsoft-cited third-party reporting. The exam launched as beta (~May-June 2026); a third-party MVP blog reports it generally available as of late July 2026, and the official certification page no longer shows a beta notice, but practice assessment remains unavailable. Duration 120 minutes from the official certification page; question count not published. Preview features may appear if commonly used. Related but separate: Microsoft Applied Skills 'Secure AI solutions in the cloud' (APL-5009, intermediate, interactive lab, study guide updated 2026-02-18) covers only (1) Defender for Cloud security for AI services (Defender CSPM for AI, workload protection plans, security policies), (2) Foundry model guardrails (content filters, blocklists, validation), and (3) Foundry environment security (users/roles, connected resources, diagnostic settings). It does not reference SC-500, does not cover Entra Agent ID, Purview DSPM, Copilot Studio, AI Gateway, and does not count toward or substitute for the SC-500 certification; it overlaps only part of the 'Implement security for AI' objective.
